Substituting B = -1/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) gives g = r/2 - r^2/(2*(1+sqrt(1+r))^2) = sqrt(1+r) - 1 (rationalized), which makes (1+g)^2 = 1+r exactly, so the pure remainder 2g+g^2-r vanishes identically for all r in [-1/2, 1/2]. Smoothness: sqrt(1+r) is C-infinity on r > -1; the chi_r support ensures 1+r >= 1/2 > 0 throughout the evaluation rectangle, so the expression extends smoothly to an open neighborhood of the closed rectangle. C=0 is the published source choice; the whole residual retains the cross term 2*u*g = O(u*r) which is not addressed by this body. Numerical confirmation from the delivered feedback: all APPLIED rows with |u| <= 1/8 and |r| <= 1/4 show abs_residual at or below 1.8e-71 (machine-precision zero), consistent with exact cancellation of the pure remainder plus negligible cross-term. Rows with |u| > 1/4 (e.g., z=0.5, z=-3, z=5) have chi_u=0 and correctly fall back to g=r/2 without invoking B or C. No NO_APPLIED_UPDATE failures occurred. Limitations: (1) cancellation is exact only at u=0; for the next stage where targets shift by tau^2*k1, u will generally be nonzero and the residual will be 2*u*g + higher-order terms, O(u*r) = O(tau^2 * tau) at most.
